sections.h2: Who sends a property tax bill to a home in Cary?
sections.html:
The county does, not the town. The Town of Cary says its limits now span three counties, Wake, Chatham and Durham, and that each county handles assessment, valuation, billing and collection for the town's tax.

Which county applies depends on where the parcel sits, so check the bill or the county's online search before you call anyone. The town page lists the numbers it wants residents to use:

  • Wake County Tax Administration, 919-856-5400. Walk-in office at 301 S. McDowell St., Suite 3800, Raleigh, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
  • Chatham County Collection Division, 919-542-8250.
  • Durham County Tax Administrator, 919-560-0300.

Wake's own page explains the arrangement: under a local agreement, the county bills and collects property tax and fees for the municipal and special districts inside Wake. A Cary owner in Wake therefore pays one bill with the county and town rates together, and anyone with questions about how the town rate was set is told to ask the town. The town also adds a $30 vehicle license fee that rides on the vehicle tax bill, with no sticker.

sections.h2: What are the Cary and Wake County tax rates?
sections.html:
The Cary rate for fiscal year 2027 is 36.75 cents per $100 of assessed value, and the Wake County rate is 53.71 cents per $100. Both are stated as printed on the official budget pages, and a bill adds the two when the parcel is in Wake.

The Cary Town Council adopted its budget at the regular meeting on June 25, 2026, raising the town rate by 2.75 cents. The same budget sets a solid waste and recycling fee of $28 per month, which is a town charge listed separately from the property tax rate. Wake's commissioners voted on June 1 for a 2-cent increase to reach 53.71 cents.

Both rates apply to the assessed value, so the value matters as much as the rate. Revaluation changes values, and the rate that follows can move in either direction. Chatham and Durham County parcels carry those counties' own rates, which you can get from the numbers above. Rates reset every July 1 with the budgets, so confirm them on the current bill instead of relying on last year's figure.

sections.h2: When are Cary property taxes due?
sections.html:
Taxes are due September 1 and can be paid at face amount through January 5. Interest starts January 6, which matches the state schedule in G.S. 105-360.

StepRuleSource
Listing periodFirst business day of January through January 31G.S. 105-307
Taxes dueSeptember 1G.S. 105-360
No interestThrough January 5G.S. 105-360 and Wake County
Interest2% from January 6 to February 1, then three-fourths of 1% a monthG.S. 105-360
Relief applicationDeadline June 1, with late filing for good cause considered case by caseWake County

Wake lets owners make partial payments of any size without prior approval, provided the balance is paid by January 5, and it sends a statement with the remaining balance after each one. Owners whose mortgage servicer pays the tax from escrow do not get a mailed bill and can look the bill up online. Wake accepts ACH or eCheck, PayPal, Venmo, Apple Pay, Google Pay and the four major credit cards.

sections.h2: How does revaluation affect a Cary home's tax value?
sections.html:
Wake County reappraised on January 1, 2024, will do so again effective January 1, 2027, and has moved to a two-year cycle after that. State law only requires a reappraisal every eighth year, so Wake revalues far more often than the minimum.

Wake's page describes four steps: neighborhooding, land and building pricing from sales, field and office review, and the notice of assessment with appeal review. It divides about 460,000 parcels into 5,400 neighborhoods and builds a Schedule of Values that the Board of Commissioners must approve. The published schedule for the 2027 round shows results presented to the Board on January 19, 2027, value notices going out by January 22, 2027, and a planned appeal deadline of April 30, 2027.

An owner who disagrees with the notice appeals to the Board of Equalization and Review. If the board rules against you, a notice of appeal to the Property Tax Commission goes in within 30 days after the board mails its decision, per G.S. 105-290. For questions on the 2027 round, Wake runs a call center at 919-857-3800.

sections.h2: What tax relief is available to Cary homeowners?
sections.html:
Wake County administers three state programs for Cary owners in its portion: the Senior and Disabled Program, Tax Deferment and the Disabled Veteran Program. Wake describes the groups as people 65 or older on a low income, people 100% disabled on a low income, and veterans with a total and permanent service-connected disability or their unmarried surviving spouses.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50% of appraised value. The Department of Revenue prints a $38,800 income limit for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker deferral: tax limited to 4.0% of income, or 5.0% above the income limit up to $58,200 for 2026, for owners with five years in the home.

Wake says the deadline is June 1 under state law, and it considers late applications case by case for good cause through December 31 of that year. Forgetting or not knowing about a program is typically not good cause. Illness, a death in the immediate family, military deployment and delay in getting disability certification are the examples it gives. Each owner can use only one of the three programs, so ask the tax office which fits. See G.S. 105-277.1 for the exclusion rules.

sections.h2: What if I cannot pay my Cary property tax?
sections.html:
Call Wake County Tax Administration at 919-856-5400 before January 6. Wake says it can set up short-term payment plans, that earlier calls leave more options, and that it cannot help once a bill becomes overdue.

State law permits past due taxes to be taken from paychecks, bank accounts or rent, and the lien on the parcel is created by G.S. 105-355 as of the listing date. Enforcement by foreclosure under G.S. 105-374 ends in a courthouse door auction, but the owner can redeem before confirmation by paying the taxes, penalties, interest and costs.

If a Cary house also has a mortgage in default, the tax lien and the lender's foreclosure can run at the same time, which narrows the timeline. Selling before an auction is set keeps control of the price with the owner, and the unpaid tax is paid from the proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: What does Cary look like for a seller?
sections.html:
Cary had 183,582 residents on July 1, 2025 per the Census Bureau, up 5.0% from the April 2020 base of 174,787. It covers 59.23 square miles of land at 2,949.7 people per square mile.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home, 2020-2024: $580,200.
  • Owner-occupied housing unit rate: 66.6%.
  • Median gross rent: $1,738.
  • Median household income: $134,905.
  • Foreign-born persons: 23.9%; bachelor's degree or higher: 70.5%.

Those numbers are from the Census Bureau QuickFacts page for Cary town. Check your value notice after each revaluation, since the assessed value is half of the tax calculation. The deed itself is recorded with the Register of Deeds in the county where the parcel sits, and Wake's office says excise tax runs $2 per thousand dollars of the purchase price.

faqs.q: Which county do I pay Cary property tax to?
faqs.a: Pay the county that holds your parcel: Wake, Chatham or Durham. The Town of Cary says each of the three counties handles assessment, billing and collection for the town's tax, and Wake's page covers the parcels inside its borders.

faqs.q: What is the Cary town property tax rate?
faqs.a: The adopted fiscal year 2027 rate is 36.75 cents per $100 of assessed value, up 2.75 cents. Wake County's rate is 53.71 cents per $100, and Wake collects both for parcels in its portion.

faqs.q: When does Wake County interest begin on Cary taxes?
faqs.a: Interest begins January 6, so paying by January 5 avoids it. The charge is 2% through February 1, then three-fourths of 1% for each month after.

faqs.q: When is the next Wake County revaluation?
faqs.a: The next one takes effect January 1, 2027, and later ones follow every two years. Wake plans to start sending value notices by January 22, 2027.

faqs.q: Can a Cary senior reduce a property tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes, if they meet age or disability and income rules. The state elderly or disabled exclusion removes the greater of $25,000 or half of appraised value, and applications are due June 1 with late good cause filings considered.
